title: What Was Charged for the Return Home
content:
What the traveller paid to come home, on an interruption claim under the Travel Protection Plans, is taken
from the carrier's ledger of the traveller's air bookings held under the Air Ticket Fare Brands, and counts only
the lines that ledger raised on an airline cancellation.

## The three readings

| What the carrier's ledger carries on an airline cancellation | What the traveller paid to come home |
|---|---|
| Both a fare charged and a change fee | The fare and the change fee together |
| Such a fare but no such change fee | That fare alone |
| Neither of those | Nothing |

A change fee raised on an airline cancellation with no fare charged alongside it does not reach either of the
first two readings, and what the traveller paid to come home is nothing. Lines the carrier raised on any other
ground are not counted here at all.

## Worked through on hypothetical figures

A fare of 742.10 and a change fee of 75.00, both raised on an airline cancellation, come to 817.10 together
under the first reading. The same fare with no such change fee comes to 742.10 under the second. A ledger
carrying only a change fee of 75.00 on that ground comes to nothing under the third.
